get.description: Search lets you search Epics and Stories based on desired parameters. Since ordering of the results can change over time (due to search ranking decay, new Epics and Stories being created), the `next` value from the previous response can be used as the path and query string for the next page to ensure stable ordering.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: See our help center article on [search operators](https://help.shortcut.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000046646-Search-Operators)

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of search results to include in a page. Minimum of 1 and maximum of 250

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description:
The amount of detail included in each result item.
   "full" will include all descriptions and comments and more fields on
   related items such as pull requests, branches and tasks.
   "slim" omits larger fulltext fields such as descriptions and comments
   and only references related items by id.
   The default is "full"

parameters.name: next
parameters.description: The next page token

parameters.name: entity_types
parameters.description: A collection of entity_types to search. Defaults to story and epic. Supports: epic, iteration, objective, story

400.description: **Either:** (1) Schema mismatch **or** (2) Maximum of 1000 search results exceeded

post.description:
Story Links (called Story Relationships in the UI) allow you create semantic relationships between two stories. The parameters read like an active voice grammatical sentence:  subject -> verb -> object.

The subject story acts on the object Story; the object story is the direct object of the sentence.

The subject story "blocks", "duplicates", or "relates to" the object story.  Examples:
- "story 5 blocks story 6” -- story 6 is now "blocked" until story 5 is moved to a Done workflow state.
- "story 2 duplicates story 1” -- Story 2 represents the same body of work as Story 1 (and should probably be archived).
- "story 7 relates to story 3”
